note: In the forty years before the Second Temple was destroyed, the signs of favor stopped: the lot for God never came up in the High Priest's right hand, the crimson wool strip no longer turned white, and the westernmost lamp of the candelabrum did not stay lit. The doors of the Sanctuary kept opening by themselves, until Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai scolded them: Sanctuary, why do you frighten yourself? I know you will be destroyed, as Zechariah prophesied, 'Open your doors, O Lebanon, that the fire may devour your cedars.'
why: The Gemara has just told how, after the High Priest Shimon HaTzaddik died, the miracles of his time faded. This continues the decline down to the destruction; the Gemara then explains why the Temple is called Lebanon, the name in Zechariah's verse.

people.name: Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai
people.about: Scolded the Sanctuary doors that opened by themselves, telling them he already knew the Temple would be destroyed.

people.name: Shimon HaTzaddik
people.about: A High Priest; during his tenure the lot for God always came up in his right hand.

terms.meaning: On Yom Kippur the High Priest drew lots to decide which of two goats was offered to God and which was sent to Azazel; the lot for God coming up in his right hand was taken as a good sign.
A red strip tied to the goat sent away to Azazel on Yom Kippur; its turning white was taken as a sign that the people's sins were forgiven.
One lamp of the Temple candelabrum that would miraculously stay lit longer than the others.
The main building of the Temple, which housed the inner holy rooms.

note: Rabbi Yoḥanan suffered from a disease called tzefidna and went to a gentile noblewoman known as a healer. She prepared a remedy for him on Thursday and Friday. He asked what he would do on Shabbat; she said he would not need it, and when he pressed her, she made him swear not to reveal the remedy. He swore, 'To the God of the Jews, I will not reveal it.' She told him, and he went out and taught it publicly.
why: The mishna cites Rabbi Matya ben Ḥarash allowing medicine to be put in the mouth of someone with throat pain on Shabbat. The Gemara then asks how Rabbi Yoḥanan could break his oath, and later explains he could treat this ailment on Shabbat because it spreads to the intestines and is dangerous.

people.name: Rabbi Yoḥanan
people.about: A Sage suffering from tzefidna who learned a healer's secret remedy under oath and then taught it publicly.

people.name: the matron
people.about: A gentile noblewoman healer who treated Rabbi Yoḥanan and made him swear not to reveal her remedy.

terms.meaning: An illness that starts in the teeth and gums, with bleeding, and moves on to the intestines.
The Sabbath, the weekly day of rest, when preparing medicine is normally forbidden unless life is in danger.

note: Rav was reading the Torah portion aloud before Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi. Each time a senior scholar walked in, Rabbi Ḥiyya, then bar Kappara, then Rabbi Shimon son of Rabbi, he started again from the beginning. When Rabbi Ḥanina bar Ḥama came in, Rav decided not to start over again, and Rabbi Ḥanina was offended. For thirteen years Rav went to him on the eve of Yom Kippur to ask forgiveness, and he would not be appeased. The Gemara explains that Rabbi Ḥanina had dreamt of Rav hung on a palm tree, a sign he would head a yeshiva, so he refused, so that Rav would go to study Torah in Babylonia.
why: The Gemara is telling stories of Sages seeking forgiveness on Yom Kippur eve. It asks how Rav could ask more than the three times Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina sets, and how Rabbi Ḥanina could refuse, given Rava's teaching that one who forgives is forgiven.

people.name: Rav
people.about: Read the Torah portion before Rabbi and, for not restarting for Rabbi Ḥanina, sought his forgiveness for thirteen years.

people.name: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi
people.about: Called simply Rabbi; the Torah portion was being read before him.

people.name: Rabbi Ḥiyya
people.about: The first scholar to enter, for whom Rav restarted the reading; the translation calls him Rav's uncle and teacher.

people.name: bar Kappara
people.about: A scholar who came in next; Rav restarted the reading for him too.

people.name: Rabbi Ḥanina bar Ḥama
people.about: Was offended when Rav did not restart for him, and refused to be appeased because of a dream about Rav.

terms.meaning: The day before the Day of Atonement, when people traditionally ask forgiveness of those they have wronged.
The leader of an academy of Torah study.
